design.decision: Whoever has the lead leads [♦] even when another suit would be the safer or stronger lead, so the team plans who will hold the lead and when to spend [♦] length.
design.opponent: Revealed on the first [♦] lead. Opponents void [♦] early so each [♦] lead runs into a trump, which makes leading [♦] cost tricks.
design.rationale: This is the length line's per-lead multiplier, with no contract scaling as the brief asks. The kept pool has [♦] lead points (common) and a three-lead milestone (common) but no uncommon [♦] lead piece. The enumerated common version (+4, e-lead-suit-d-mult) measured +8.2 inside the band and was cut only because the common pool already covered it, so this shape is proven and the uncommon slot gives room for a larger amount. A lead trigger pays even when the trick is lost, so it rewards owning the suit instead of winning with it, which separates it from the win payoffs.
